problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Y∼N(-1,{2}^{2}),$ compute $P(Y\ge 1).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8413\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8643\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8849\,$ | $\,0.8869\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ |

$P(Y\ge 1)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-1$ and $\sigma =2.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 1) & =P(Z\ge \frac{1-(-1)}{2}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 1)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/4cdc40bd57d5f855afa08ee21b3bb9eeeefca8c09bd4d857cf3f3b2514693110.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 1) & =1-P(Z<1) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1) \\  & =1-Φ(1)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(1)=0.8413.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 1) & =1-Φ(1) \\  & =1-0.8413 \\  & =0.1587.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge 1)=0.1587.
$$
